chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from the one who mentioned him, from Bashir al-Dahhan who said: I heard Abu al-Hassan Musa (peace be upon him) saying:
Verily, God — Majestic and Mighty — detests the servant who sleeps much and is idle.

key_terms.الفارغ: al-Farigh — the idle, the empty, the one devoid of occupation or purpose
key_terms.النوّام: al-Nawwam — one who sleeps excessively; habitual sleeper
key_terms.يبغض: yubghidu — to hate, detest, hold in abhorrence (divine aversion, stronger than mere dislike)

ai.seo_question: Does God hate laziness and sleeping too much in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kadhim (peace be upon him) declared that God abhors the servant who spends his time in excessive sleep and idleness. This teaching addresses the socioeconomic and spiritual danger of laziness and inactivity — in a society where livelihood depended on active labor and moral engagement, wasting time in sleep or idle leisure was a form of ingratitude and neglect of one's duties to God and community. The terms 'al-nawwam' (habitual sleeper) and 'al-farigh' (the empty/idle one) evoke someone who has abandoned both worldly responsibilities and spiritual vigilance.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from the one who mentioned it, from Bashir Al Dahhan who said, 
‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> saying:
‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Majestic and Mighty Hates the sleeping and the leisurely servant’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from the one whom he has mentioned (in his book) from Bashir al-Dahhan who has said the following: “I heard abu al-Hassan, Musa, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ’
Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, dislikes an excessively sleeping servant who passes his time without work.’”
